column1: # THE ONE CLASSING OF build/'s TOP-LEVEL DIRECTORIES (#304, 14z-207; maintainer-ruled 2026-10-23, "Adopt all four
# (Recommended)"). Read by tools/build_dirs.py; tools/static_confirm.py's N-D scratch rule and its pruned untracked
# listing are GENERATED from the `scratch` rows, never written a second time (written twice, the glob
# `build/agent[0-9]*/**` and the regex `agent\d+\w*` disagreed on build/agent7-x/ and build/agent7.d/).
# Census: tests/test_build_dirs.sh — every build/<top> that tools/ and tests/ programs name, and every build/ top-level
# directory present, must be classed here, or the gate fails.
# class<TAB>pattern<TAB>reason. A pattern is ONE path component: a glob of `*`, `?` and `[...]` (git's glob magic).
# A name's class is the first of scratch, input, kept, fixture with a row matching it; a name matching a scratch row
# and a row of another class fails the census (the planner's split must be unambiguous).
#   scratch  the session tooling's own output: no static gate reads a file under it (PILOT trace, #313/#304); the
#            planner judges it by R4 alone (N-D) and the planned snapshot change (#304 item 2) would leave it out
#   input    a gate or a tool reads it (a program names it, or the PILOT trace saw a read)
#   kept     a build or session output nothing is known to read; judged by every rule, as before
#   fixture  named only inside a gate's synthetic repository or message; never a real directory of this tree
# Top-level FILES under build/ (logs and the like) are out of this list's scope; the planner judges them as before.
